new_page.title: How Much Is Property Transfer Tax in BC? 2026 Rates & Examples
new_page.h1: How much is property transfer tax in BC?
new_page.description: BC property transfer tax is 1% of the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus 2% on homes over $3 million. Worked examples inside.

breadcrumbs.name: How much is property transfer tax in BC?

faq.q: Is property transfer tax paid on the assessed value?
faq.a: No, on the fair market value at registration. For an ordinary sale that is the price you paid. BC Assessment values are used only for sales that are not on the open market, such as transfers between family.

faq.q: Can I add property transfer tax to my mortgage?
faq.a: Generally no. It is a closing cost paid in cash through your lawyer or notary, so budget it with your down payment.

parts.t: Property transfer tax in BC is 1% of the first $200,000 of the fair market value, 2% of the part from $200,000 to $2,000,000, and 3% of the part above $2,000,000. Homes over $3,000,000 pay a further 2% on the residential value above $3,000,000. On a $900,000 home that is $16,000.

items.t: A further 2% on the residential value above $3,000,000 (only the residential part of a mixed property)

parts.t: The tax is worked out on the fair market value on the day the transfer is registered at the Land Title Office. In an ordinary open-market sale that is the purchase price.

blocks.text: What it costs at common prices

parts.t: The buyer pays it, as part of closing. Your lawyer or notary files the return and pays the tax when the transfer is registered, so you need it in cash on top of your down payment. Your mortgage does not cover it.

First-time buyers can save up to $8,000 on homes up to $835,000 (fully exempt up to $500,000). Buyers of a newly built home that will be their home pay nothing up to $1,100,000. Foreign buyers pay an extra 20% in the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
